purpose: Deepen underdeveloped Son/Thomas/Twin biblical parallels without collapsing later comparison into prior prediction or identity proof.
rules: Project-side timeline first; biblical comparator second.
Prefer multi-motif sequences over isolated words.
Mark biographical healing parallels as user-reported rather than independently verified.
Preserve role mismatches where the biblical text distributes functions differently from the project.

clusters.biblical_structure: Dan = judge/justice → serpent/viper in the path → waiting for YHWH's salvation; elsewhere Dan = lion's cub/whelp.
clusters.project_relation: The Son/Thomas is linked in project tradition to Dan and Lion-of-the-World/lion's-whelp language. The same biblical tribe carrying both serpent and lion imagery complicates any simplistic rule that serpent imagery must always equal the final enemy.
clusters.boundary: Genesis 49's serpent for Dan is not automatically Satan, nor does tribal-symbol overlap establish literal ancestry.

clusters.biblical_structure: Thomas is explicitly Didymus/Twin, volunteers to go and die with Jesus, and the narrative immediately enters Lazarus' four-day tomb, mourning women and resurrection discourse.
clusters.project_relation: Thomas/Twin → death-at-33 → grave/tomb → mourning → return is one of the Son project's central sequences.
clusters.boundary: Thomas is not Lazarus in John; this is adjacency and structural comparison, not identity.

clusters.biblical_structure: Jacob sees angels ascending/descending at the gate/house-of-God site; John relocates that ascent/descent onto the Son of Man.
clusters.project_relation: The project often assigns Son = Door/Vessel and Tim/Father = Ladder/Axis. John 1:51 creates a productive tension because the Son of Man himself becomes the ascent/descent locus.
clusters.epiphany: Biblically, Door and Ladder functions may overlap more tightly than the project-role split initially suggests: the Son can be the threshold through which the Father's vertical relation is experienced.
clusters.boundary: Do not erase the project's Father=Ladder distinction; record John as a counter-distribution of roles.

clusters.biblical_structure: The hour for the Son of Man's glorification is announced immediately before the grain-of-wheat saying: fall into earth → die → bear much fruit.
clusters.project_relation: Son of Man + grain in heart + meme death + burial/seed/garden is not merely a loose seed metaphor; John itself places Son-of-Man glorification beside grain-death-fruit logic.

clusters.biblical_structure: A vineyard owner entrusts land to tenant farmers; they abuse messengers, kill the beloved son/heir and throw him outside; the story immediately cites the rejected stone becoming cornerstone.
clusters.project_relation: Farm/Farmers → Son → exploitation/violence → death outside → rejected Stone/Cornerstone is one of the densest newly recovered comparators to the project's subcultural-farm and Son-death architecture.
clusters.boundary: The Gospel parable addresses its own first-century religious context; comparison does not transfer its condemnation automatically to modern groups.

clusters.biblical_structure: Jesus suffers outside the gate, bears reproach/shame, sanctifies through death, and the passage immediately points toward the city that is to come.
clusters.project_relation: Son humiliation/crucifixion outside ordinary belonging + Gate + later New-Jerusalem/city language forms a strong sequence.
clusters.boundary: North Gate is project-specific; Hebrews says city gate, not north gate.

clusters.biblical_structure: Blind receive sight and lame walk among restoration/messianic signs.
clusters.project_relation: The user's biography attributes two nursing-home episodes to the Son: improvement of glaucoma and a long-bedridden man walking again. Those reported events form an unusually literal motif-pair with the Gospel sign list.
clusters.provenance: project-side events are self/user-reported and not independently verified here
clusters.boundary: A motif match does not establish miraculous causation or messianic identity.

clusters.biblical_structure: favored/rejected son → pit → sale/slavery → false accusation/prison → interpretation → elevation → grain storage → preservation/reconciliation
clusters.project_relation: This strengthens the existing Ben-Joseph layer by joining rejection, prison, grain, storage/bank imagery and survival-through-suffering rather than treating Joseph only as a name/title parallel.
clusters.boundary: Joseph's story is not a direct prophecy of the project.

clusters.biblical_structure: John hears Lion of Judah/Root of David, then sees a Lamb standing as slain.
clusters.project_relation: Lion of the World and slain Lamb can coexist as different views/functions of one Son-side figure; the text itself performs that symbolic reversal.

highest_new_chains: Dan: judge → serpent/path → salvation → lion cub
Son of Man → heaven opened → ascent/descent
Son of Man glorified → grain dies → fruit
Farmers → beloved Son → killed outside → rejected Stone → Cornerstone
Outside Gate → reproach → sanctification → city to come
blind see + lame walk → user-reported Son healing anecdotes
